@claude we need to show the use of quick disconnects for backs of trays (I know for sure there are some things like this available, including for gas and liquid, not just power). It's also possible to do something that I've explored before of using retractable cabling, which could include gas and liquid lines, which would allow for continuous connection. This would get tricky for really tall systems (though that could be a matter of keeping that kind of equipment lower), and it introduces some additional engineering challenges. Use of a UPS for power is the alternative that we've already been considering. We can also have N2 generators and potentially self-contained chilled water, but with all of these heat management becomes even more of a concern. Anything involving disconnects, we'd probably want to have it be temporary, i.e., only during transport, with an automatic connect happening in the picking bay, too.

I want to see the entire lab getting set up from scratch as well, including installation of arms, loading of all equipment onto the trays, etc.

I also want you to look through DAL at all the workflow steps we're doing to help see what kinds of things we're going to need to do. Add sieving off the powder that comes out. There might be an automated sieving module of some sort, otherwise you can show the robot arm doing manual sieving.

Pull in a VHX microscope too, one with the elemental characterization module with the laser. Probably something about that here or on DAL.

Add desktop XRF if you haven't already

Put one more openflexure (6 total). Instead of freestanding, put them in an array on some kind of sub-tray with cutouts to make it look a bit less weird.

I was picturing the rail being close to the floor with a pedestal (to make maintenance and usage of the other equipment easier for when we power off the rail), but I'm realizing that also means less repeatability from the pedestal being able to sway back and forth. So, I'm not sure. This kind of gets me thinking back towards mobile manipulator. Show a version that assumes a mobile manipulator in more of a warehouse setting.

I think I have a link (maybe to YouTube? Maybe my personal youtube channel?) showing my testing with a real VLM which I'd like to have on hand. If not standalone, there's almost certainly that in one of my presentation videos, such as the foundation models one I gave that's on YouTube (not sure if this was on my own account or not).

Upload the recent videos to YouTube, including anything you do here. I'll do a claude-youtube ping for putting them into a playlist.

I want to see the actual workflow of pulling one of the plates out of the Aconity MIDI and bringing it over for wire EDM, then taking the tensile specimen and putting it in the tensile tester

I also want to see an automated packaging station with automatic label creation and fixturing (i.e., for sending out powders)

I also want you to add the stream cameras that we have been using throughout here, powder-doser, robot-arms, etc. You can use a Pi 5 design with the two cameras: HQ camera and a wide angle. Should these be mounted to the modules themselves or to the trays? I'm not sure. But there should definitely be an overhead one above the trays when they're in their picking position. Let's assume there's some separate mounting that occurs but that is per-tray where there can (and should be) multiple streaming setups per tray.

Plan out and show cabling for all of this, i.e., wired power connections (you can keep these tidy).

The CubXL should be the setup adapted for corrosion testing (see DAL)

I want rendered visualizations for each of the machines and demonstrations of full workflows (where you show what's actually happening on the inside, fading out what's around it, to show certain workflows occurring, and wherever possible, pulling in real data such as SEM images for these)

Could a hot isostatic press fit on the VLM?

You should also put a DED machine (not sure which one, maybe MX Lab or maybe FormAlloy or maybe something else; see DAL around bronze DED and that ONR proposal) that's freestanding outside the VLM

You can open up new stacked PRs to trigger subagents for whatever you'd like here.

You seem to be missing something. We can atomize far more than 80 grams. We load multiple charges into the crucible (4), and potentially much more if we upgrade to the 400 cm^3 crucible

Aside: I'm pretty sure there are bay sizes that are close to 1000 mm, as a Kardex option. I can probably dig some of this up, but check ac-dev-lab first for mention of this. Look a little harder, see if you can find one of the extended Kardex brochures somewhere. Use the Pi if needed

For all those collisions and interferences, couldn't you use something like mujocu (sp?) to simulate this?

The idea would be to have the robot take care of this, or to use something more automated. We can add a second robot arm if needed, or have some kind of clamping mechanism or clever hardware-centric design similar to what's been explored in robot-arms with the powder dosers. You can probably come up with something like that, that would work for dealing with the sieves. I think Gage might have taken a video of our sieving process and put it on YouTube already.

> * The doser's funnel doesn't fit a cup

The doser typically isn't supposed to have or use funnels, though we did use some for what we were doing in dosing the charge cups (paper funnels). Why in the world does the doser have a load cell? We would be using an HR-100A or whatever it is, and the larger capacity version that still has 0.1 mg resolution (I forget what this is, but it's mentioned on powder-doser I think, maybe on a borysgroup repo). Either way, we should be fine here.

### The larger bay: Modula has one, up to 1,295 mm

The larger bay size is **Modula's**, not Kardex's. It is in the *Modula Lift Brochure* that Outsource Equipment sent on Mar 27, 2026. me-madsen attached that email to [issue 53](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/byu-vcl/issues/53) as [`Vertical.Lift.Information.-.Outsource.Equipment.eml`](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26388212/Vertical.Lift.Information.-.Outsource.Equipment.eml), and the brochure PDF is inside it. Its bay table is on page 10.

**Modula Lift bays, maximum product height**

| Bay | Single delivery | Dual delivery |
|---|---|---|
| S | 695 mm (27.36") | 320 + 320 mm |
| M | 895 mm (35.24") | 320 + 520 mm |
| **XL** | **1,295 mm (50.98")** | 320 + 920 mm |

- **The MC models take the same tray as our Modula quote:** 2,500 × 857 mm. Load per tray is 500 kg on the MC50D, 750 kg on the MC75D and 990 kg on the MC1000D.
- **The Apr 2 Modula quote** (MC50D, external bay) lists "Usable Height Per Tray: 27.36 in.", so it is priced with **Bay S**. An M or XL bay would need a requote.
- **Kardex:** 727.5 mm is still the only figure anywhere. It is in the Shuttle 500 spec sheet in AccelerationConsortium/vlm-justification (`tech-specs.png`, "Maximum Product Height 727.5 mm"). The Apr 2 Hoj Engineering quote for the Shuttle 500 (2450 × 864 × 3850) gives no product height. Box, OneDrive, local files and the ac-dev-lab archives (issues 216, 372 and 471) have no taller Kardex opening.

**What the bigger bays would fit,** using the heights from the earlier rounds:

- **Bay M (895 mm):**
  - fits the Mastrex MX100 (800 mm), the Fusion X (860 mm), the N₂ generator (889 mm), the MX-Lab (835 mm) and an open Form 4 (844 mm);
  - doesn't fit the MetalONE or the DiMetal-100 (1000 mm each).
- **Bay XL (1,295 mm):**
  - fits everything above, plus the MetalONE and the DiMetal-100;
  - still doesn't fit the Meltio M450 (1400 mm), the MPRINT (1900 mm) or the HIP (1300 mm and 1100 kg);
  - the Instron 68SC-2 should be checked against 1,295 mm.
- **Load:** the MX-Lab's 250 kg on 0.47 m² points to an MC75D or MC1000D tray, or a spreader plate.

**The vibration data** asked about in round 4 are in AccelerationConsortium/vlm-justification: `vibration_data.csv`, `cleaned_vibration_data.csv` and `vertical-lab-vibration-data-VBA01001-analysis.xlsx`, with `plot_vibration.py`. The Kardex, Modula and MSK test plots are in ac-dev-lab issue 216.

**Next step:** re-fit the trays against a Modula MC75D or MC1000D with a Bay M and a Bay XL opening (2,500 × 857 mm tray), and ask Outsource Equipment to requote the MC with a Bay M or Bay XL.

@claude-super see the many many comments below. You'll want to spend some extra time in advance trying to make a plan and organize things. Many of these relate to another PR, and you will be posting claude pings on new and existing PRs as a result of this (because you are claude-super). When you make a new PR or when you post a claude ping to another PR, you should include max 300 characters and a link to the PR in your final comment reply here, and put the nitty gritty details in a comment on the PR or in a new PR description. You have a 6 hr walltime, both for this job and for new jobs that you trigger. Try to keep in mind CPU limits and concurrency so you and sub-pings don't get killed prematurely.

Noting that the overhead planning layouts (2D) around 2:50 show overlap between certain modules and the UPS

The OT-2 is empty

Are all modules within the VLM currently, 120 V? Do some have higher power requirements?

5:56 shows a rail still. We moved fully over to the mobile manipulator setup, no?

Considering a swap to mostly or all security cameras (with lots of adjustability in terms of angle, resolution, night vision, onboard temperature/humidity logging, etc.) with a Pi 5 handling the streaming and control (similar to https://github.com/borysgroup/aurora-cloud-infra/pull/35, but doesn't have to be that brand, and I also need an approximate cost here - open a new PR focused on that). Look into multiple types of security cameras; there's probably no need for that kind of shielding around it (i.e., without the dome or whatever) and I'm guessing there are different sizes of security cameras, and ways to mount it from the tray, the top of the module, sides, etc. I.e., flexibility and freedom in mounting. Ideally, easily adjustable. Perhaps some security cameras come with built-in temperature and humidity sensors. If not or that limits other features, then no problem (see below). Note that for a security camera, the power requirements might be higher than what a typical Pi 5 charger would handle. So, consider the wattage as well in the assessment. Not sure if it's actually quite low or somewhat high. Btw, I'm not saying change everything to a security camera. You can leave the current RPi cam setups in the animations. I'm intending you to open a PR focused on this instead.

Each tray should have an airgradient added to it for environmental monitoring. Each station should also have one

It's still showing the picking bay as being "open top". In real kardex systems, I'm pretty sure there's a "roof" to the bay. For this reason, I don't think that 2020 bar is needed (6:27) and the camera could be mounted

We can also have multiple overhead cameras in the bay to get different angles (e.g., ceiling middle back, ceiling middle front)

At 6:42, it's not worth showing both the wide and the HQ. Perhaps though, going back to a motorized security camera, if the security camera had a really good zoom, maybe we could have two side-by-side, one focused on wide capture and another that could point closely at whatever workflow is happening. Keeping in mind also that there would be a gripper camera too. And we should probably add two or three cameras to the mobile manipulator (one on either side, on that's situated higher up, maybe on some kind of rod or extrusion, mimicking the three cameras described in https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/robot-arms/pull/40). Open another PR related to that, adding cameras to the mobile base

Do we have ICP-MS as a module? If not, we should. Also, an OT-2 probably doesn't have great compatibility with many of the solvents that would be required for ICP-MS and ICP-OES. And it would be very risky to try to put high-hazard chemicals on a tray. This would be better for a standalone fumehood, and probably with a liquid handler that's designed for those kinds of harsh solvents (maybe Hamilton? Really expensive, but we need good chemical compatibility..). On a similar note, we might need a similar kind of sleeve or protection for the UR arms. Also, I think UR10e-s have been replaced by UR12e-s (apparently a rebrand of the UR10e maybe?). Not sure if that affects the CAD model, but the naming should probably be updated throughout, which will be a big lift to try to do this **everywhere** and might lead to confusion when trying to reuse historical content where UR10e is fixed.

On a related note, the combitac should probably have a port for vacuum, ideally a decent level of vacuum (not sure if turbo would make sense, but maybe the option to use roughing with optional switch to turbo, kind of like the T85 turbo pumping station, but not necessarily that one specifically, since it probably doesn't have the right capacity - also that we'd probably want to use a scroll pump to reduce noise post-startup). Note that this port would be optional on a per-tray basis, but included in the picking bay for trays that require it.

For the CubXL, would it make sense to put both a P20 and a P300 onboard? It seems like there are a lot of small transfers to fill things up, and I worry a bit about evaporation (you could run some basic calculations related to that?). Maybe it's fine though. Or maybe an Opentrons Flex pipette (5-1000 uL). Open a new PR related to this.

We should also probably use something more robust than the Ag/AgCl reference electrode (and there are probably some that require far less maintenance)

Throughout the various workflows, we also need to be thinking about automatic floor cleaning (e.g., a roomba-like device adapted to use an explosion proof vacuum) which could maybe be it's own (3rd) MiR250 that has an explosion-proof vacuum and works in tandem with one of the mobile manipulators as needed. At that point, could be worth just putting a UR12e on it anyway.. Idk.. open a new PR for me to explore that idea further.

Potentiostat is mispronounced in the narration. Look for other hiccups like that in the narration. "MiR" should be pronounced "meer" (common pronunciation). 

17:28, holding the lid down while working the latch seems unnecessary? It's also still missing the typical "unlatching" step that has to happen before pulling the latch down.

18:06 I'm confused how the loading tong is designed and how it works.

19:21 - we're working on automating the other aspects of the atomizer. This should be replaced with the latest we have there in terms of automation.

20:05 - that's not my video. That's from AMAZEMET. 

20:26 - that's not a good photo. That's aluminum slag/scrap. You should be able to find a better jar photo for the Al atomizer runs.

21:12 the atomizer is missing the new renders in other spots across the video.

The VLMs here seem.. short. We could probably assume taller VLMs. See #344 for context. Not going to be 50', but maybe something closer to 30'. Kardex made it sound like building higher at a later stage is also feasible. This affects many other things, like the overhead facilities (power, etc.).

9:54, when it's actually on the pedestal, it still looks relatively unsecure.

The dose is still going from way too high up. We probably need more of a custom breeze break that extends higher up. Either way, that's way too long of a fall distance before it lands in the cup. EDIT: I'm seeing this described in 16:13 as well. Again, I think you need a custom breeze break. Also seems like maybe you could reverse the orientation of the balance to free up space (again, with a custom breeze break).

11:43 "most by hand" is dissatisfying and misleading. For example, coating the crucible is being explored as automated in another PR (either here or in DAL) I'm pretty sure.

11:46 - is this not some simplified version compared to the tray setups from before? I thought there were more trays. Maybe I'm wrong here.

We should probably automate machining of the high-purity cups and plugs. Do we have automated machine shop-type stations already? Open a new PR focused on the automated machining aspect. This would also need to include a cleaning and drying step (IPA for example).

Also the die punch and that whole setup probably needs a way for it to be cleaned in-between presses. I worry about cross-contamination from one run to the next in terms of powder.

We should probably be weighing the cups again after doing the press fit.

Noting for the atomizer automation, we can probably have the two arms working together to adjust the position of the plate in real-time during the several minutes of atomization.

23:59 arm collision with atomizer

Cross-contamination for the anti-static brush is going to be a concern.. how to handle that? Thorough cleaning? (e.g., ultrasonic cleaning). Disposable heads? (e.g., kind of like disposable wand attachments in other contexts).

24:58 I think there was a collision here, too. There's also not much of an automation-friendly grip for the gripper. Seems like it would slip out. 

25:53 the text on the sign bleeds off the edges. Nice on having a ground cable and ground bar or similar. I wonder about trying to have a mobile ground bar of sorts (overhead), or maybe better, just making sure ground is available within close reach pretty much anywhere nearby machines or where the mobile manipulator would be.

We also need to consider waste and disposal procedures. Where does this go? How do we get pickups for waste? Can we do something to minimize the hazard/risk (and thereby also cost of disposing it)? Open a new PR focused on this.

This is as far as I got. Will need to pick back up another time.

Do we have ICP-MS as a module? If not, we should. Also, an OT-2 probably doesn't have great compatibility with many of the solvents that would be required for ICP-MS and ICP-OES. And it would be very risky to try to put high-hazard chemicals on a tray. This would be better for a standalone fumehood, and probably with a liquid handler that's designed for those kinds of harsh solvents (maybe Hamilton? Really expensive, but we need good chemical compatibility..). On a similar note, we might need a similar kind of sleeve or protection for the UR arms. Also, I think UR10e-s have been replaced by UR12e-s (apparently a rebrand of the UR10e maybe?). Not sure if that affects the CAD model, but the naming should probably be updated throughout, which will be a big lift to try to do this everywhere and might lead to confusion when trying to reuse historical content where UR10e is fixed.

On a related note, the combitac should probably have a port for vacuum, ideally a decent level of vacuum (not sure if turbo would make sense, but maybe the option to use roughing with optional switch to turbo, kind of like the T85 turbo pumping station, but not necessarily that one specifically, since it probably doesn't have the right capacity - also that we'd probably want to use a scroll pump to reduce noise post-startup). Note that this port would be optional on a per-tray basis, but included in the picking bay for trays that require it.

For the CubXL, would it make sense to put both a P20 and a P300 onboard? It seems like there are a lot of small transfers to fill things up, and I worry a bit about evaporation (you could run some basic calculations related to that?). Maybe it's fine though. Or maybe an Opentrons Flex pipette (5-1000 uL). Open a new PR related to this.

We should also probably use something more robust than the Ag/AgCl reference electrode (and there are probably some that require far less maintenance)

Throughout the various workflows, we also need to be thinking about automatic floor cleaning (e.g., a roomba-like device adapted to use an explosion proof vacuum) which could maybe be it's own (3rd) MiR250 that has an explosion-proof vacuum and works in tandem with one of the mobile manipulators as needed. At that point, could be worth just putting a UR12e on it anyway.. Idk.. open a new PR for me to explore that idea further.

Potentiostat is mispronounced in the narration. Look for other hiccups like that in the narration. "MiR" should be pronounced "meer" (common pronunciation).

17:28, holding the lid down while working the latch seems unnecessary? It's also still missing the typical "unlatching" step that has to happen before pulling the latch down.

18:06 I'm confused how the loading tong is designed and how it works.

19:21 - we're working on automating the other aspects of the atomizer. This should be replaced with the latest we have there in terms of automation.

20:05 - that's not my video. That's from AMAZEMET.

20:26 - that's not a good photo. That's aluminum slag/scrap. You should be able to find a better jar photo for the Al atomizer runs.

21:12 the atomizer is missing the new renders in other spots across the video.

The VLMs here seem.. short. We could probably assume taller VLMs. See #344 for context. Not going to be 50', but maybe something closer to 30'. Kardex made it sound like building higher at a later stage is also feasible. This affects many other things, like the overhead facilities (power, etc.).

9:54, when it's actually on the pedestal, it still looks relatively unsecure.

The dose is still going from way too high up. We probably need more of a custom breeze break that extends higher up. Either way, that's way too long of a fall distance before it lands in the cup. EDIT: I'm seeing this described in 16:13 as well. Again, I think you need a custom breeze break. Also seems like maybe you could reverse the orientation of the balance to free up space (again, with a custom breeze break).

11:43 "most by hand" is dissatisfying and misleading. For example, coating the crucible is being explored as automated in another PR (either here or in DAL) I'm pretty sure.

11:46 - is this not some simplified version compared to the tray setups from before? I thought there were more trays. Maybe I'm wrong here.

We should probably automate machining of the high-purity cups and plugs. Do we have automated machine shop-type stations already? Open a new PR focused on the automated machining aspect. This would also need to include a cleaning and drying step (IPA for example).

Also the die punch and that whole setup probably needs a way for it to be cleaned in-between presses. I worry about cross-contamination from one run to the next in terms of powder.

We should probably be weighing the cups again after doing the press fit.

Noting for the atomizer automation, we can probably have the two arms working together to adjust the position of the plate in real-time during the several minutes of atomization.

23:59 arm collision with atomizer

Cross-contamination for the anti-static brush is going to be a concern.. how to handle that? Thorough cleaning? (e.g., ultrasonic cleaning). Disposable heads? (e.g., kind of like disposable wand attachments in other contexts).

24:58 I think there was a collision here, too. There's also not much of an automation-friendly grip for the gripper. Seems like it would slip out.

25:53 the text on the sign bleeds off the edges. Nice on having a ground cable and ground bar or similar. I wonder about trying to have a mobile ground bar of sorts (overhead), or maybe better, just making sure ground is available within close reach pretty much anywhere nearby machines or where the mobile manipulator would be.

We also need to consider waste and disposal procedures. Where does this go? How do we get pickups for waste? Can we do something to minimize the hazard/risk (and thereby also cost of disposing it)? Open a new PR focused on this.

This is as far as I got. Will need to pick back up another time.
